issue.title: [service] Enabling the process resource detector aborts collector startup (slice-valued resource attribute)
issue.body:
### Component(s)

`pkg/service` (`service/telemetry/otelconftelemetry`)

**Describe the bug**
Enabling the `process` resource detector via the resource-detection config added in #15226 makes the collector fail to start. Startup aborts with:
```
failed to create resource: <Invalid value type []string>
```

**Steps to reproduce**
`service::telemetry::resource`:
```yaml
service:
  telemetry:
    resource:
      detection/development:
        detectors:
          - process: {}
```
The collector fails to start every run.

**What did you expect to see?**
The collector starts and the `process.*` resource attributes (including the slice-valued `process.command_args`) are attached to internal telemetry.

**Root cause**
`createResource` (`service/telemetry/otelconftelemetry/resource.go:110`) copies each detected SDK attribute with `pcommonAttributes.PutEmpty(k).FromRaw(kv.Value.AsInterface())`. For a slice attribute, `attribute.Value.AsInterface()` returns a typed Go slice (`[]string`, `[]int64`, `[]float64`, `[]bool`), but `pcommon.Value.FromRaw` only accepts `[]any` for slices (`pdata/pcommon/value.go`) — a typed scalar slice hits the `default` branch and returns `<Invalid value type %T>`. `createResource`'s error aborts `service.New` (`service/service.go:150-153`). The `process` detector always emits `process.command_args` as a STRINGSLICE (from `os.Args`), so it fails deterministically; any detector emitting a typed-slice attribute fails identically.

**Not a `FromRaw` bug:** `pcommon.Value.FromRaw`/`AsRaw` are a deliberately `[]any`-symmetric pair (`AsRaw` returns `[]any` for slices; PR #6579). The fix belongs at the caller, matching the existing `ToZapFields` SDK-attribute converter (`internal/telemetry/attribute.go`), which type-switches on `attribute.Value.Type()`.

### Collector version

v1.62.0/v0.156.0 (the release that shipped #15226) and `main` (`fe96e04e8`)

prompt.pr_title: [service] Fix startup panic when a resource detector emits a slice-valued attribute
prompt.pr_body:
<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Enabling the `process` resource detector (or any detector emitting a slice-valued resource attribute) aborts collector startup with `<Invalid value type []string>`. `createResource` fed the OTel SDK attribute value directly into `pcommon.Value.FromRaw`, which only accepts `[]any` for slices — typed scalar slices (`[]string`/`[]int64`/`[]float64`/`[]bool`) hit the `default` error branch and abort `service.New`.

This converts slice-typed SDK attributes element-wise into a `pcommon` slice, mirroring the existing `ToZapFields` SDK-attribute converter (`internal/telemetry/attribute.go`, which type-switches on `attribute.Value.Type()`). Scalar and other types keep the existing `FromRaw` path. The `pcommon.FromRaw`/`AsRaw` `[]any`-symmetric contract (PR #6579) is intentional, so the fix is caller-side rather than in pdata.


<!-- Issue number if applicable -->
#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #15571

<!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.-->
#### Testing
Added a `TestCreateResource` subtest exercising the `process` detector; it asserts the collector resource is built and `process.command_args` is a proper element-wise slice equal to `os.Args` (not a stringified `"[...]"`). Red before the fix (`<Invalid value type []string>`), green after. Full `service/telemetry/otelconftelemetry` module passes with `-race`.


<!--Describe the documentation added.-->
#### Documentation

No changes.

issue.title: Extract storage configuration for components into a separate module
issue.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Components need to use storage extensions for various purposes. There should be a standard way of configuring storage for a component, given the potential for multiple storage extensions coexisting.

See the following contrib issue for examples and some discussion: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/10915.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should add a `configstorage` module similar to `configauth` which defines the configuration, and which other components can then use. For the actual configuration, explicitly setting the storage like it's done here:  seems to be the consensus. For example:

```yaml
extensions:
  filestorage/example1: {}
  filestorage/example2: {}
receivers:
  filelog:
    storage: filestorage/example1
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: <ENDPOINT>
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      storage: filestorage/example2
```

**Additional context**
The following contrib issue was where the discussion started: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/10915.

issue.title: [config/configtls] Document possible goroutine leak caused by TLSServerSetting
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
This was caused by #6708 with the introduction of the feature that reloads the client CA file. When a `LoadTLSConfig` [is called](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/c64ac69dacdc9c1dc2c8c0e47e8ffdbe5464f295/config/configtls/configtls.go#L300) for `TLSServerSetting`, the Client CA [reloader starts watching](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/c64ac69dacdc9c1dc2c8c0e47e8ffdbe5464f295/config/configtls/configtls.go#L311) the file for changes, [using a goroutine](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/c64ac69dacdc9c1dc2c8c0e47e8ffdbe5464f295/config/configtls/clientcasfilereloader.go#L96). The method to stop this goroutine is to call [`shutdown()`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/c64ac69dacdc9c1dc2c8c0e47e8ffdbe5464f295/config/configtls/clientcasfilereloader.go#L133) on the reloader.

As a part of #9220 I've added a public method `Shutdown` on `TLSServerSetting`. This method must be called on shutdown by every user who has opted to enable the `client_ca_file_reload` [option](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/c64ac69dacdc9c1dc2c8c0e47e8ffdbe5464f295/config/configtls/configtls.go#L102), otherwise a goroutine leak will occur.

This config option is currently not documented anywhere (outside of code) and is disabled by default, so the impact at this point should be small. Enabling this option opens the door to more leaks happening to unsuspecting users in components that may not already have similar shutdown calls, so I'd appreciate input on what to do here.

prompt.pr_title: [pkg/config/configtls] Don't leak a goroutine for client CA reload
prompt.pr_body:
<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

Previously `configtls` would use `fsnotify` and create a goroutine that had no way to be stopped to observe the CA contents have changed. This changes the `configtls` to use the same logic it does with the server TLS watching to check on each `getClientConfig`.

This leaking is bad for collector restarts in process, as it will create a new goroutine each time. This only gets worse with the new partial reload work where if a receiver is using `configtls` on each restart it would leak a goroutine.

<!-- Issue number if applicable -->
#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #9221

<!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.-->
#### Testing

Add tests coverage for all scenarios of file changing, unreadable, etc.

<!--Describe the documentation added.-->
#### Documentation

Didn't change any documentation as the result is the same, just removes the leak.

issue.title: [cmd/builder] `--skip-get-modules` shouldn't regenerate `go.mod`
issue.body:
### Component(s)

cmd/builder

### What happened?

**Describe the bug**
When you call `ocb` with `--skip-get-modules`, it correctly skips the `go mod tidy` step. However, it still regenerates the `go.mod` file. This means that the subsequent build that occurs after that will inherently need to make the same jump of `go mod tidy` that you want to avoid with that flag in the first place.

**Steps to reproduce**
Use `--skip-get-modules` feature.

**What did you expect to see?**
My `go.mod` to maintain the updates I had made to it, such as `go get`ing a specific dependency I want to keep patched up in my build.

**What did you see instead?**
The `go.mod` was regenerated from the template, essentially creating an untidied `go.mod` file with the base dependencies that `ocb` can figure out, which will then be resolved the same way a `go mod tidy` would when you run the build on it.


### Collector version

v0.153.0

### Environment information

## Environment
OS: Any
Compiler(if manually compiled): go1.26.2


### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml
N/A
```

### Log output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional context

This is related to my work about making `ocb` useful when you need the generated source code to live for a long time. The big thing I want to enable is to be able to run `ocb` to update templates without blowing away the `go.mod` updates that have already occurred. This is particularly useful if you're patching a dependency and want to update the `version` of your binary, but don't want to blow away the patches your `go.mod` may already have.
